lastCompletedStory.title: Recover post-merge via git pull --rebase, never reset --hard

nextStoryContext: runPostMerge's Step 1 is now `git pull --rebase origin main` (never --reapply-cherry-picks, never reset --hard). PostMergeOutcome's ok:false branch is now `{ ok:false; reason:string; completedSteps:string[]; remainingSteps:string[] }`, built by a private `failAt(step, reason)` helper over `const ALL_STEPS = ['checkout','pull-rebase','tag','prune','close']` (completedSteps = steps strictly before the failing step; remainingSteps = the failing step + everything after). Every failure reason populates these fields consistently: checkout-main-failed, rebase-failed (renamed from pull-failed), version-file-read-failed, version-parse-failed, tag-create-failed, tag-push-failed. prune/close never appear as a failing step (both best-effort/non-fatal, can't produce ok:false). US-003 (next) wires post-merge-stalled-marker.ts (US-001) into the sidecar: write the marker using these exact completedSteps/remainingSteps + reason fields when a post-merge run fails/stalls, remove it once a subsequent run completes cleanly (ok:true), and read it for the boot-read/recycle-recovery blocker line in templates/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md (that template edit + embed-vendor is US-003's own scope, not started here). runPostMerge itself still does not write the marker (no claudeDir in scope) -- the sidecar caller does that in US-003. src/release/merge-watch.ts's handleMergedStatus only reads `result.reason` on failure today; it does not yet read completedSteps/remainingSteps -- that consumption is exactly what US-003 adds.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed git rebase (and therefore `git pull --rebase`) drops clean cherry-picks of already-upstream commits by DEFAULT via patch-id comparison (git log --cherry-mark), which is exactly the subsumed-local-commit drop this story relies on. --reapply-cherry-picks forces reapplying those commits instead of dropping them, confirming the notes' instruction to never pass it. No reset --hard used anywhere in the implementation.
